faqs.q: What are kraft coffee sleeves used for?
faqs.a: Kraft coffee sleeves are used to reduce heat transfer from a hot cup to the customer’s hand. They make drinks easier to carry, improve grip, and help prevent accidental burns during takeaway service. They also provide a clean branding space without changing the cup itself.

faqs.q: Do kraft coffee sleeves fit all cup sizes?
faqs.a: They can be produced in multiple dielines to fit common sizes like 8oz, 12oz, 16oz, and 20oz cups. Fit depends on the cup’s top and bottom diameter, not just ounces. Sharing your cup dimensions helps match the sleeve shape to a snug wrap.

faqs.q: Are kraft coffee sleeves better than double cups?
faqs.a: Sleeves reduce the need to double-cup in many service situations, which can lower material use and improve speed. Double-cupping adds cost and can still feel slippery with condensation. A well-fitted sleeve provides insulation and grip in one step.

faqs.q: Can I print my logo on kraft coffee sleeves?
faqs.a: Yes, printing can be added for logos, brand names, QR codes, or short messages. Kraft surfaces work best with strong contrast and clean spacing so text stays readable. Print placement should avoid folds and seams where artwork can distort.

faqs.q: Will printing look different on kraft material?
faqs.a: Kraft paper naturally softens color brightness compared to white stock. Dark inks and simple designs usually appear clearer. If brighter tones are needed, an underlayer or specific print approach can improve contrast while keeping the kraft look.

faqs.q: Do kraft coffee sleeves help with grip?
faqs.a: Yes, kraft sleeves add texture and thickness, which improves grip compared to a bare paper cup. This is especially helpful for customers walking, driving, or carrying multiple drinks. Some sleeves can also include light embossing for extra hold.

Many kraft sleeves are recyclable when they are primarily paper-based and don’t use heavy plastic laminations. Local recycling rules can vary, so it’s best to align sleeve finishes with your area’s recycling acceptance. Minimal coatings generally support easier recycling paths.

faqs.q: What thickness should I choose for a sleeve?
faqs.a: Thickness depends on drink temperature, cup material, and how long the drink is held. Higher GSM kraft can feel more protective for very hot drinks. A balanced thickness also helps the sleeve keep shape and stay tight on the cup.

faqs.q: Do sleeves slide or rotate on cups?
faqs.a: A properly sized sleeve should stay in place and resist rotation. Sliding usually happens when the dieline doesn’t match the cup taper or the seam isn’t tight. Adjusting the sleeve geometry for your cup model fixes most fit issues.

faqs.q: Can kraft coffee sleeves be used for iced drinks?
faqs.a: They are mainly designed for hot drinks, but some brands use them for grip on large cold cups as well. For iced drinks, condensation behavior matters more than heat insulation. If you want sleeves for cold cups, sizing and moisture resistance should be planned accordingly.

faqs.q: How do cafés store sleeves efficiently?
faqs.a: Sleeves are typically packed flat in stacks, which saves storage space compared to bulky cup accessories. Keeping them dry and away from steam areas helps maintain their shape and print quality. Many cafés store stacks near the espresso line for quick access.

faqs.q: What’s the difference between kraft sleeves and white sleeves?
faqs.a: Kraft sleeves provide a natural brown appearance and often align with eco-forward branding. White sleeves can make colors appear brighter without an underlayer. The best option depends on your brand look and the printing style you prefer.

faqs.q: Can I order kraft coffee sleeves in bulk?
faqs.a: Yes, bulk ordering is common for cafés, chains, and event suppliers to maintain consistent sizing and print runs. Bulk quantities also help keep packaging uniform across locations. Planning one approved dieline makes reorders simpler over time.

faqs.q: Do sleeves work on ripple cups or double-wall cups?
faqs.a: Sleeves can still be used on ripple or double-wall cups, but fit must be checked because wall thickness changes the cup diameter. Some cafés skip sleeves on insulated cups, while others use sleeves for branding and grip. Testing one sleeve size against your cup style is the safest approach.

faqs.q: What should I share to get the right sleeve made?
faqs.a: Share your cup size (oz), the top and bottom diameter, and a photo or link to the cup model if possible. Also share your print needs and whether you want a plain kraft look or highlighted branding areas. This helps lock a dieline that fits snugly and prints cleanly.
